conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is Samuel Grant with the Internal Revenue Service Taxpayer Refund Division. Am I speaking with Mr. Carter?
Yes, this is Allen Carter. I own Carter's Flooring. Is there a problem with my taxes?

Thank you, Mr. Carter. No problem per se, but I'm contacting you regarding your recent tax filings for your business. Our records indicate you are eligible for a government refund of $3,600 under the Small Business Relief Act.
A refund? I wasn't expecting that, to be honest. I thought my taxes were all sorted.

Yes, after recalculating your 2022 and 2023 returns, we've determined an overpayment in your federal business taxes. However, before the IRS can issue your refund, federal guidelines require a one-time clearance fee to verify your identity and process the disbursement.
Wait, I have to pay a fee to get my own refund? That seems odd. Is this standard procedure?

I understand your concern. Due to an increase in tax fraud, the IRS has implemented this temporary verification process for all business refunds over $2,000. The clearance fee is $289, fully refundable once your identity is confirmed and your refund is processed.
Alright. How do I pay the clearance fee?
For your convenience, we accept payment via Zelle, direct bank transfer, or by prepaid Visa cards. Which option works best for you today?
I guess I could do Zelle. What's the Zelle address?
Excellent. Please send the $289 to irs.refunds@federalservicesmail.com through Zelle. Once you initiate the payment, please confirm the transaction ID with me.
I'm not sure I have that much in my Zelle account right now. Can I use a credit card instead?
Absolutely, Mr. Carter. You may use a Visa, Mastercard, or American Express. I am authorized to securely take your card details and process the clearance fee directly.
Shouldn't I just pay this on the IRS website? I usually pay my taxes there.

The IRS website unfortunately does not accept identity verification payments for refund processing. As per Section 431-B, third-party payment is required to prevent refund fraud. This is a temporary, legally mandated step.
Alright, if you say so. Do you need my card info now?
Yes, please. For security, I'll need the card number, expiration date, and the three-digit code on the back. This information is encrypted and used solely for the clearance fee.
Alright, my card number is 4512 3456 7890 1122, expiration 04/27, and the code is 932.
Thank you. I'm submitting your payment now. Please remain on the line while I process your clearance.
Okay, I'm here. How long will this take?
Just a moment. Also, for confirmation, can you verify the business address associated with your IRS filings?
Yes, it's 1229 Garfield Ave, Suite 4, Springfield.

Thank you, that matches our records. I'm now unlocking your refund process. However, if the clearance fee is not approved within the next thirty minutes, federal refund eligibility may be revoked, and your case flagged for audit.
What? Audit? I've kept everything in order, I can't have an audit right now.

I understand, Mr. Carter. To avoid complications, it is imperative the clearance fee is settled now. If your payment does not go through, you may also visit a nearby CVS or Walgreens and purchase two $150 Vanilla Visa gift cards as an alternative.
So if my card doesn't work, I buy two $150 gift cards and give you the numbers?
Correct. Once you purchase the cards, scratch off the back and read me the numbers. That will immediately confirm your identity, and your refund will be released to your business account.
Alright, I can do that if my payment doesn't go through. Will I get a confirmation for all this?

Absolutely. You will receive an official IRS confirmation email and your refund deposit receipt once the clearance fee is processed. Please let me know if you have any issues with your card or obtaining the gift cards.
